independentReview.reason: APPROVE, first round, no blocking findings, and the record should be specific about what that verdict rests on: all nine assigned checks were run by execution rather than read from this PR's prose. It verified the head with git ls-remote before starting. It reproduced the central urgency claim by checking out main in a fresh clone, running git fetch origin --prune, and running the audit, which FAILED citing exactly the two claimed reasons, then confirmed OK at this head. It measured the receipt blob off the git object rather than the checkout, immune to CRLF distortion, matching 9c8bcc4400ddebd633ed9c94245951694d91abaf / 71 lines / 10473 bytes, and cross-checked its contents against live GitHub: PR #345's headRefOid matches the receipt's currentHead, and its merge commit has exactly one parent, confirming the squash the receipt narrates. It verified the #345 record's honesty from the outside, finding the literal 'This does not fix #341.' in the pushed message of e5197e5b, confirming #341 still OPEN, and confirming the landed squash message carries zero keyword matches -- proving that repair was actually applied on GitHub and not merely described. Most usefully, it did not accept the omitted-SHA reasoning as plausible: it PATCHED docs/BRANCH_DISPOSITIONS.md in its scratch worktree to add the citation, reran the suite, watched it go 49/49 to 48/49 failing exactly the pinned squashOnlyCitations assertion with {pr:345, sha:'109cb284'} appearing unexpectedly, and reverted. Two non-blocking observations, both ruled non-blocking BY THE REVIEWER and neither hidden here. First: it could reproduce only 61 of 63 guards, the two failures being rules C and D of scripts/handoff-worktree-truth.test.mjs, which assert live local machine state -- actual worktree count and local branch resolution. It proved these environmental rather than caused by this diff by rerunning the identical tests against origin/main in the identical scratch clone and getting the same two failures for the same reason, and neither file is touched by the diff. Its fair caveat stands in the record: the 63/63 claim is credible as a writer-machine result but cannot be reproduced test-for-test off this specific 33-worktree machine, by those tests' own design. Second: a third variant of the --all hole beyond the two disclosed, structurally inherent and not introduced by this PR -- git rev-list --all resolves refs from EVERY remote configured on a writer's machine, not specifically origin, so a receipt pushed only to a fork would satisfy the guard there while remaining invisible to a fresh clone of the canonical repository. The PR's disclosure of 'these are the holes' is therefore slightly incomplete, and that correction is being filed on #341 rather than left in a review transcript.
